The three primary machine learning algorithms that were employed to predict the kind of crime that would occur given other factors were K Neighbors Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, and Logistic Regression. The accuracy was moderate to low. The Random Forest Classifier, Logistic Regression, and K Neighbors Classifier displayed an accuracy of 52.55%, 43.86% and 38.39%. Nevertheless, by displaying past crime data trends, law enforcement officials can identify crime hotspots, identify emerging trends, and allocate resources efficiently. This would enable law enforcements to anticipate and prevent crimes before they occur, allowing for proactive interventions.

articleTitle: QR CODE ENCRYPTION USING LU DECOMPOSITION AND PCA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The Quick Response (QR) code, a machine-readable optical label, is a pattern two-dimensional of black and white blocks. At present its applications extend to various domains, including message sharing and document authentication, etc. It can store critical and important information through the encryption of data. It can store essential information through the encryption of data. The increased utilization of QR codes also raises concerns regarding privacy and security issues related to the information they contain. This project explores the combination of mathematical methods in computing, including LU Decomposition and Principal Component Anal-ysis (PCA), to devise a robust encryption approach. LU Decomposition, a matrix factorization technique, disintegrates a matrix into lower and upper triangular matrices. On the other hand, PCA is a statistical procedure utilized for dimensionality reduction. The results highlight the effectiveness and efficiency of em-ploying LU Decomposition and PCA for encryption, reinforcing QR code security.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of VSC Controllers: Discrete PWM vs Improved Hysteresis PWM for Voltage Sag Improvement in Grid-Connected Hybrid PV-Wind Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This study compares discrete pulse width modulation (PWM) and improved hysteresis PWM controllers for voltage sag mitigation in grid-connected hybrid PV-wind power systems with dynamic voltage restorers (DVRs) based on battery storage and superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES). The analysis focuses on the controllers' effectiveness in maintaining voltage stability and reducing total harmonic distortion (THD) under various grid conditions. Simulation results show that while both controllers effectively mitigate voltage sags, the improved hysteresis PWM demonstrates superior performance in terms of THD reduction and dynamic response. The findings provide insights into selecting optimal VSC controllers for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of grid-connected renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Hydro-Sentinel: Flood Water Observation and Extraction System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In regions prone to flooding, such as Chennai, managing floodwater is a critical challenge, especially during heavy storms and rainfall. This project, titled Hydro-Sentinel: Flood Water Observation and Extraction System, addresses this challenge by proposing a comprehensive solution comprising floodwater monitoring and dewatering systems. The monitoring system, based on IoT and embedded systems, continuously monitors water levels and sends SMS alerts to users’ mobile devices when floodwaters breach critical thresholds, enabling timely intervention. Additionally, the dewatering system automatically extracts floodwater once it reaches predefined levels, utilizing level sensors, controllers, and motors. By integrating real-time monitoring and automated dewatering capabilities, Hydro-Sentinel offers an effective solution to mitigate the impact of flooding, preventing water stagnation and minimizing damage to infrastructure and property. The main objective is to eliminate the need for human involvement, Hydro-Sentinel offers a robust solution to mitigate flooding effects, ensuring timely action and reducing the risk of property damage and infrastructure disruption.

articleTitle: Design of Advanced Integer and Non-Integer Controller for Islanded Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In this paper, an approach for the design of controller for networked islanded microgrid system integrated with distributed energy resources, electrolyser system, energy storage system and fuel cell will be developed. The controller design process will consider network-induced time delay in the synthesis of PI controller. The gain margin and phase margin specifications will also be considered to ensure a robust design. Microgrid system have gained significant attention in recent years due to their ability to integrate distributed energy resources and support sustainable and reliable electricity generation. In islanded microgrid systems, since the Microgrid operates autonomously in a floating mode without any integration to the main power system grid, it is crucial to develop advanced control strategies that can ensure stable and reliable operation. The closed loop system will be modelled in transfer function approach. For step change in load, the incremental frequency variable will be studied to visualize the impact of control. In the analysis, the variations caused by the photovoltaic cell and wind due to environmental conditions will be considered to assess the robustness of designed control. The MATLAB based simulation studies will supplement analytical results.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Human Emotion Using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Human emotions are the mental states resulting from neurophysiological changes that are diversely linked to human thoughts, feelings, and behavioral reactions. Facial expressions, eye movement and gestures are several nonverbal communication methods used in many human-machine interactions. Facial emotion recognition has been an essential field because it has many applications that convey the mental state and emotions of each individual. As there is no clear way to distinguish between emotions on a face and the complicated neural system that is connected to the face, recognizing human emotions is a difficult undertaking. In this paper, for students' facial expression recognition, we presented a model called Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The proposed model consists of six convolutional layers, six max pooling with two fully connected layers. Using a Haar cascade detector, the system identifies the faces of students from input images. It categorizes them into seven different facial expressions, including surprised, fearful, disgusted, sadness, happiness, anger, and neutral. The FER2013 dataset yielded an accuracy rate of 77.22% for the proposed model. The comparative study is carried out with four other deep learning models. The models are Inception V3, VGG-16, VGG-19, Resnet50 and the accuracies achieved are 40%, 37%, 22.50%, 22.09%, respectively.

articleTitle: Unsolicited Email Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Spam emails, commonly known as junk emails, are unsolicited messages sent in bulk to numerous recipients. These messages typically inundate email inboxes and can range from annoying promotional content to potentially harmful phishing attempts and malware distribution. This work presents a comprehensive approach to email classification and sentiment analysis. It begins by preprocessing email data, encompassing lowercasing, punctuation removal, tokenization, and stemming. The study uses Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Naive Bayes models to classify emails as spam or ham with machine learning. The accuracy of these models is evaluated and compared, with SVM demonstrating the highest accuracy. Sentiment analysis is performed using the V alence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning (VADER) tool to evaluate email sentiment. This work also generates word clouds to visually represent the most frequent terms in both input mail and the dataset.

articleTitle: Analysis of Virtualization Based Approach for Detecting Computer Network and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The Research presents a virtualization-based method and system for establishing network security services. It includes the following steps: acquiring host devices and computing node sets. based on the host's equipment, determine the link bandwidth; The set of host devices and computing nodes is used to build the computing resource model. The service function chain is implemented using the computing resource model to create network security services. This paper presents a strategy that leverages the features of container-borne network functions for quick deployment, and it suggests several dynamic function deployment techniques. Based on the concept of integer programming optimization problem modeling, the overall problem is broken down into separate sub problems, the optimization problem's scale is reasonably constrained, and quick container deployment is used to guarantee that service request response times are minimal while, to some extent, retaining the performance advantages of simple optimization methods.

articleTitle: Investigation of Decentralized Autonomous Blockchain Enabled Platform for Crowd Funding
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This research presents a way to crowdfunding that improves security, trust, and transparency in the process by utilizing smart contracts and blockchain technology. The method gives contributors a significant say in project choices by utilizing tokenization and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). The report places special emphasis on how important fraud prevention, transparency, and identity verification are in the crowdfunding environment. A thorough case study demonstrates the advantages of decentralization, transparency, and security in the context of a decentralized equity crowdfunding process. It highlights how blockchain-based crowdfunding might change the crowdfunding industry and emphasizes its disruptive potential. There is potential for both project creators and backers in this paradigm change towards decentralization and transparency, which also has wider ramifications for the digital age finance ecosystem. The proposed system is implemented as a web application and integrated with the Ethereum and meta mask platforms for simulation.

articleTitle: Modeling Virus Mutation and T-Cell Dynamics in HIV/AIDS: A Comparative Study using Finite Difference and Physics-Informed Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In order to meet the biological constraints, In this paper we consider a system of four equations which captures T-cell-HIV interactions. It describes the behavior of normal T cells, latently-infected T cells, actively infected T cells and virus with special emphasis on reclassification, death rate and population dynamics. The model makes sure that the sum total of T-cell population is bounded while its steady-state solution remains stable. This document symbolically provides basis for stability conditions resulting from HIV's impact on CD4+T cell numbers.

articleTitle: Tackling E-Waste Management Using Decentralized Marketplace Leveraging Ethereum Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This study explores the implementation of a decen-tralized marketplace using blockchain technology for e-waste management. Through stakeholder-driven validation using the proof of stake and on-chain attestation, the platform ensures transparency and accountability in the e-waste supply chain. Integrating the Meta Mask wallet facilitates secure transactions, enhancing user experience and adoption. Results demonstrate a 95% reduction in transaction confirmation time and a 25% cost reduction in Ethereum transactions compared to SWIFT transfers, enhancing economic viability and user engagement. Leveraging blockchain for e-waste management presents a promising avenue for addressing complex supply chain challenges and advancing toward a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Various Division Algorithms for Image Processing Applications - A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Division is one of the most commonly sort after algorithm for performing image processing operations such as normalization, filtering, enhancement, deconvolution etc. Hence, the design of efficient division algorithm is highly essential in order to obtain a better image processing algorithm The first and foremost step in the implementation of any algorithm in hardware is to identify the number systems used to represent the inputs and outputs. The inputs, outputs and complexity of the algorithm varies based on the number system used. This paper proposes a recursive subtraction based fixed-point division algorithm. This work also provides a comparative analysis on various aspects such as area, power, delay and throughput, on comparing the proposed recursive subtraction based fixed-point division algorithm with the existing floating-point division, restoring integer division and non-restoring integer division algorithms and operator based fixed-point division algorithm.

articleTitle: EmotiGuard: Real-Time Human Emotion Recognition System for Adult Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The emotion recognition IoT system proposed in this study was developed to check the individual's emotion state and health status. The aim of this research is to create an efficient but accurate system for real-time emotion detection. An edge computing based system was adapted in this research, and the hardware used was Jetson Nano, a small and fast edge device with a low-energy ARM CPU, which was integrated with an RGB camera for capturing an image. The RGB camera captured images when it detected the persons and the Haar feature-based cascade classifiers extracted the face regions surrounding the detected persons. The pre-trained model MobileNet for the human recognition, which was trained already on a GPU machine, classified the detected persons. The face region around the detected individual and the identified human face image was sent to the server where the MobileNet deep learning model was implemented to check the emotion of the persons detected by face classification. This study provided extensive results with more accurate human identification and effective emotion recognition. This study tested more than 500 samples which also advances the state-of-the-art in the emotion recognition by integrating edge computing for real-time processing and achieved higher accuracy in human identification and emotion detection.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation and Components Importance Measure of DC-DC Charging System of EVs with Different Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Present day transportation system use increasingly use of electric motor than conventional IC (combustion) Engine. EVs are developing on very fast pace and they also face challenges such as reliability, availability, and safety of these systems. In this paper reliability modeling evaluation of DC-DC charging system of EVs has been carried out. A new measure, droop reliability of DC-DC charging system of EVs using three different capacitors has been computed. Also component importance of different components of DC-DC charging system of EVs using Birnbaum's importance measure has been carried out.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to MicroorganismImage Analysis Using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new deep-learningbased framework for the automatic analysis of microorganism images in MATLAB. In fact, this is an effort to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the microorganism classification method using the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach. Our dataset was very inhomogeneous, containing many different images of microorganisms, so we first normalized with respect to image quality and size. We then developed, balancing between model complexity and computational efficiency, training our custom-made CNN model. We quantitatively evaluate our model by using rigorous experiments with standard metrics of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The experimental results of our model could provide following accuracies: the model has an accuracy of 83.78%, precision of 83.88%, recall of 86.72%, and, hence, an F1 score of 84. Such metrics point to the high reliability of the model in the process of microorganism identification, possibly with a slightly higher level of recall pointing to fewer false-negative cases in the classification of the biological entity. Further analysis suggests that in addition to becoming a strong solution for the classification of microorganisms, our model also becomes a strong basis for the following such research. Future work could integrate larger datasets, transfer learning, and even deploy the model in a real clinical setting. Our work shows the possibilities of applying deep learning with MATLAB as a powerful stronghold for the development of microorganism image analysis, which is critical in many applications aimed at the health care, environmental monitoring, and biological research fields.

articleTitle: Transformer-Less High Step-Down Converters with Reduced Device Count: Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Transformer-less DC-DC converters are crucial in various applications, especially when a high step-down voltage transformation is required. This paper comprehensively reviews the transformer-less DC-DC converters, focusing specifically on the reduction in the number of inductors, capacitors, and switches. This paper provides the limitations of conventional buck converters. An in-depth analysis explores each topology's converter structure, advantages, and limitations concerning high step-down requirements. Moreover, the review delves into the recent advancements and emerging trends in transformer-less DC-DC converter designs modified for high step-down applications. Special attention is paid to efficiency considerations, size constraints, total number of components, and stresses on switches, and the comparative analysis is presented in this paper. This review intends to help people make better decisions and inspire new ideas in power electronics, specifically focusing on high step-down voltage conversions.

articleTitle: EEG Emotion Prediction Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Emotions are fundamental for human beings and play an important role in human cognition. Emotion is commonly associated with logical decision making, perception, human interaction, and to a certain extent, human intelligence itself. Emotion detection discussed in this paper is a technique that uses electroencephalography (EEG) to measure brain activity and identify different emotional states, it is a non-invasive method that measures electrical activity in the brain through electrodes placed on the scalp. The electrical activity of the brain is related to different cognitive and emotional processes, and electroencephalography can be used to measure changes in brain activity that occur in response to different emotions. The emotion prediction model can be used for early detection and of mental health disorders and to tailor personalised treatment plans for such patients, to help researchers gain a better understanding of the emotional aspects of various conditions and even in stress management, wellness program and more.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of GaN-Based DC-DC Converter for Solar Application in a DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a Gallium Nitride (GaN) based DC-DC converter for solar application in a DC microgrid environment. The superior characteristics of GaN devices, such as high switching speed and power density, the developed converter aims to enhance the overall performance and efficiency of the microgrid system with solar PVs. In this paper, the comprehensive simulation studies are followed by hardware prototyping and experimental validation. Key design considerations encompass GaN device selection, converter topology, and control strategy. Performance evaluations include transient response characterization under varying operating conditions. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed GaN-based converter in facilitating power conversion within solar-based DC microgrids, thereby contributing to the advancement of sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Models for Multi-Event Classification of Vibrational Patterns in Distributed Acoustic Sensing System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The phase-sensitive optical time domain reflectometer has extensive vibration detection applications in various domains. It can detect multiple vibrational event patterns due to its distributed sensing nature. Effectively classifying these events based on their features holds significant importance in distinguishing between different types of vibrations. This work focuses on showcasing the exceptional characteristics of various machine learning models for event classification, prioritizing computational efficiency and reduced processing time. The emphasis is also placed on the judicious selection of features to optimize classification accuracy. In this work, a publicly available dataset with six vibrational events was chosen and the classification of events was performed using three machine learning-based classifiers - Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbor, and three machine-learning gradient boosting algorithms - Extreme Gradient Boosting, Categorical Boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine. Some of the key hyper-parameters of the algorithms were also varied to understand the trade-off between the accuracy and computational complexity of the models. The Light Gradient Boosting Machine achieved the highest accuracy of 95% with fewer estimators and computation time, which was evaluated by the appropriate tuning of the hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Encrypt Decrypt ReLU Activated UNet Prototype based Prediction of Leaf Disease Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The issues of sustainable agriculture and climate change are intimately linked to the problem of effective leaf disease prevention. In practice, the primary method for identifying and detecting plant diseases is expert observation with the unaided eye. However, this necessitates for the ongoing supervision of specialists, which can be too costly for big farms. The automatic identification of leaf diseases is a significant area of research because it might be useful for monitoring vast agricultural fields and identify diseases based only on symptoms that occur on the leaves of the plants. This paper recommends ReLU Activated UNet (RAA-UNet) that categorizes the leaf diseases with high precision. The KAGGLE Leaf disease Dataset that contains 2094 leaf images were used for implementation. The dataset consists of 1047 leaf image and 1047 respective leaf images that have been segmented. The proposed ReLU Activated UNet initiates by creating masked leaf images by masking the original image with a segmented leaf image. To classify the leaf disease, the masked leaf images are assigned to ReLU Activated UNet with contracting and expansion which was activated using Relu Activation function. The proposed ReLU Activated UNet and conventional CNN models are fitted to the masked leaf images. As demonstrated by the experiments, the proposed ReLU Activated UNet model works better with a high accuracy of 98.85% in the classification of leaf disease like leaf spot, blight and powdery mildew.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Lung Cancer Prediction Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, necessitating advanced diagnostic tools for early detection and intervention. This project introduces a novel approach to lung cancer prediction by leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) on lung X-ray images. The CNN model is trained to classify lung X-rays into four categories: adenocarcinoma, large cell carcinoma, normal, and squamous cell carcinoma. The methodology involves preprocessing of lung X-ray images, feature extraction using CNN layers, and classification through a carefully designed neural network architecture. The model's training is based on a dataset encompassing a diverse range of cases, facilitating robust learning and accurate predictions. The significance of this project lies in its potential to enhance early detection and streamline diagnosis, leading to timely medical interventions. By automating the categorization of lung cancer types through CNN analysis of chest X-rays, this system aims to contribute to the efficiency of healthcare services and improve patient outcomes. The evaluation of the proposed model involves comprehensive performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and precision. Results from extensive testing on diverse datasets showcase the model's efficacy in distinguishing between various lung cancer types and identifying normal cases.

articleTitle: Hazard Hunter: A Low Cost Search and Rescue Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Rescue operations are among the most vital pillars of disaster management. The duties associated with rescue operations or monitoring in such situations are exceedingly risky. Besides, human participation in such endeavors is invariably hazardous. As a result, as the probability of human error and the need for manual labor diminished, robot involvement gained importance. On the contrary, before human rescue teams embrace robotic assistance, individuals must be confident that it will benefit them rather than hinder them. Considering these issues, an affordable search and rescue robot (SARR) ‘Hazard Hunter’ is proposed and designed to suit developing nations like Bangladesh. This robot is cheap and straightforward to build from common components. Human rescuers may easily exploit the robot's information without any robotic expertise. One notable benefit of this robot is that it can perform remote operations via a wireless way. Sensors, along with a camera module, are incorporated into the design of the automaton to provide real-time information about the terrain around it and enable adequate surveillance. As required, the user may add or remove sensors and access those sensor's readings via web-based monitoring. The development of a user-friendly IP address-based webpage accomplishes the movement of the robot and the acquisition of sensor data for environmental monitoring. It provides continuous thermal, visual, and ambient sensory data from the catastrophe site to the online dashboard. It can also find live people amid debris and communicate with rescuers. The proposed rescue robot has undergone extensive experiments and performance-based evaluation. It will effectively carry out its responsibilities in any critical circumstance.

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: - In this research, we present DRNet, a deep learning model for automated detection and grading of diabetic retinopathy (DR) using fundus images. DR is a leading cause of vision loss in diabetic individuals, emphasizing the importance of early detection. Our model combines the ResNet architecture for feature extraction with the U-Net architecture for lesion segmentation. Trained on a large dataset of 666,383 fundus images from 121,342 diabetic patients, DRNet incorporates realtime image quality assessment, lesion detection, and grading of DR severity. Evaluation on both local and external datasets, totaling 409,455 images, demonstrates the effectiveness of DRNet, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC) of 0.90-0.936 for lesion detection and 0.96-0.98 for DR severity grading. Our results suggest that DRNet has the potential to enhance DR screening programs by improving accuracy and efficiency in diagnosis, thereby benefiting patient outcomes and healthcare systems.

articleTitle: CodeSense: Code Summarizer for JavaScript
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In many software projects, especially large and complex ones, there often exists a significant gap in documentation. This can lead to a lack of understanding among developers, especially when they encounter unfamiliar code or need to debug and maintain legacy systems. By building a code summarizer model, developers can automatically generate concise and informative summaries for different sections of code. These summaries serve as on-demand documentation, providing clear explanations of the code's purpose and functionality, making it easier for developers to navigate, maintain, and extend the codebase. So, for making the job for the developers simple we have built this code summarizer model which will help the developers to understand the purpose and functionality of different parts of the code. Automatically generated comments can serve as an initial draft for code documentation, making it easier to keep documentation up to date.

articleTitle: An Optimized Analysis of Electrical Activity of a Respiratory Muscles Using Advanced Surface Electromyography (sEMG)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is an effective tool for measuring electrical activity of the respiratory muscles in patients receiving prolongation mechanical ventilation (MV) support and for individuals experiencing acute respiratory problems. However, the utilization of sEMG sensor in clinical applications and research is still limited due to a lack of transparency and standardization in the demonstration procedure, as well as the information regarding the data acquisition method (including the pre-processing stage of filtering and motion artifacts), important clinical parameters to take into consideration for data interpretation and processing is still a challenging task. Therefore, in this paper we present a simple cost effective data acquisition hardware and software model to analyze the electrical activity of a diaphragm muscle using sEMG sensor and Arduino UNO WiFi R3 module. The sEMG sensor is used to acquire the electrical signal from the diaphragm muscle, whereas, the Arduino module processes the data obtained from the sensor, and the WiFi module sends the data to an Internet of Things (IoT) platform for real-time visualization and interpretation, allowing the end user clinical experts to diagnose patients' conditions. Further, we considered non-invasive bioimpedance analysis to assess the patient's condition in a time-efficient manner.

articleTitle: Electric Field Control in Polymeric Insulators by Optimizing Shed Location and Functionally Graded Material
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Though composite insulators are gaining popularity in the power system networks, their failures due to electric field induced corona and local discharges pose a serious threat to their service duration. Electric field across the insulator should be limited below the threshold value to prolong the insulator life. This paper analyses the effect of Functionally Graded Material (FGM) on reducing electric field magnitude at the critical locations of the composite insulators. Finite element method is used for electric field computation and analysis. The introduction of FGM reduces the electric field at all critical locations of the insulator. The influence of FGM geometry and its relative permittivity is also studied. Additionally, the location of the first shed near the high voltage electrode of the insulator is also optimized for reduce electric field magnitude. Locating the first shed nearer to the first shed, increasing the thickness and relative permittivity of the FGM considerably reduce the electric field magnitude.

articleTitle: CropBot: A Chatbot for Agriculture Advancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: India is an agriculture-based country in that 82 percent of farmers are small scaled and less exposed to diverse knowledge. So, we developed chatbot which helps farmers in giving advises on what crop they have to grow according to the soil nutrients and environmental parameters. With the dataset ‘crop recommendation’ from Kaggle we created a chatbot with the help of machine learning and NLP to find which crop will be giving best yield according to the soil nutrients like nitrogen, potassium and phosphorous and environment factors like temperature, humidity, pH of soil and rainfall. With the help of NLP, we created a user-friendly chatbot which is developed to access and chat easily by a less knowledgeable person also. The chatbot is developed in such a way that the sentences are not needed to be well phrased and step by step our chatbot only will assist the user. Chatbot will give recommendation even the user doesn't have complete information with either soil nutrients or environment parameters the chatbot can give recommendations. This project aims to help farmers with accessible data driven solutions for crop's greater yield.

articleTitle: Suno.G: A Comprehensive Assistive Communication Framework for the Specially Abled
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In response to the communication challenges faced by the specially abled, who comprise around 5% of the global population, we present Suno.G-a dedicated application designed to bridge the communication gap. With a primary focus on the deaf and dumb community, Suno.G strives to empower users through a thoughtfully crafted and intuitive interface. This interface seamlessly integrates text and visual aids, fostering effective message conveyance. Users engage with the application by typing out messages, a transformative process wherein the text undergoes translation into sign language or is visually represented through a dynamic array of images and icons. Suno.G pioneers inclusivity by offering a spectrum of customization options, including font size, color preferences, and the provision of a quick-access repository for frequently used phrases. These features collectively contribute to an enriched user experience, tailored to individual needs and preferences.

articleTitle: Dynamic Traffic Management and Prioritization for Emergency Vehicles using IoT-enabled Density Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: - The project's goal is to create a density-based dynamic traffic signal system that can adjust the signal's timing based on the amount of traffic at any particular junction. As traffic congestion is a major problem in the majority of cities around the world, keeping smart traffic flow on the roads is essential as it helps both citizens and security agencies. The traffic signals continuously turn green or red, and the signals for traffic need to change based on how many vehicles are present in the area. The green lights should be on longer in situations where there is a lot of traffic going in one way, and the red lights should stay on longer in situations where there is less traffic. The first should be given to emergency vehicles like ambulances and fire extinguishing engines. Consequently, the idea suggested here is a system in which the length of the green and red light timings is controlled by the volume of traffic at that particular time. If an emergency vehicle is in a lane, that lane is cleared before any other. The implementation of IoT technology is key to our solution. It allows for wireless connectivity between devices that can be monitored and controlled from anywhere, at any time. We use this technology to connect IR sensors that measure the density of vehicles on the road. Additionally, a camera takes pictures of emergency vehicles which are processed in the server by using image processing techniques where the image is processed and calibrated so that signal is sent to the server. The information about emergency vehicles and the density of traffic on each road is then sent to a microcontroller, specifically the ESP32. The microcontroller uses this information to determine the optimal time for green lights, thereby reducing traffic and pollution.

articleTitle: Identifying The Established Semantic Kinds In Text Using Named Entity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Named entity recognition (NER) is a natural language processing (NLP) method that extracts information from text. NER includes identifying and ordering significant data in text known as named elements. By approaching span-based method (where tokens are represented as spans) we can detect named entity for each span. However some current algorithms check every span separately without knowing previous span, which leads to ambiguity. To overcome this, a bi-directional two-dimensional operation is used, which uses knowledge of previous spans and compares the two spans and generates meaningful named entities. For implementation of the NER we have used the three public datasets. The experimental results in this paper shows that the method we used is very effective to generate meaningful nested named entities.

articleTitle: Cascade Neural Network Based MPPT Controller for Thermoelectric Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The thermoelectric generator (TEG) converts heat energy into electrical energy. The electrical power generated from TEG largely depends on the difference in the junction temperature of the TEG. The maximum power generated from the TEG varies when temperature difference varies. The efficient controller has to be designed to track the maximum power under varying temperature conditions so that the TEG always operate at the maximum power point for better efficiency. This paper proposes a novel neural network approach using cascade architecture for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) in TEG. The proposed method is compared with conventional feed-forward neural network based MPPT controller in terms of accuracy and complexity. The interesting and promising results obtained are presented.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Power Distribution from Electric Vehicles: Enabling Rural Electrification and Sustainable Mobility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This study introduces a transformative approach to utilizing electric vehicles (EVs) as dynamic power transport solutions for underprivileged households, with a focus on three-phase power systems. The innovation lies in a versatile converter system that enables the charging of light electric vehicles (LEVs) from both AC and DC power supplies while simultaneously powering rural household appliances directly from the LEV battery. The converter incorporates an active bridge-based single-stage three-phase AC/DC converter with an auxiliary DC port, reducing the high-frequency switch count needed for efficient power conversion. This system operates in three distinct modes: charging the LEV battery from a three-phase AC grid, charging from another EV or battery, and directly powering household appliances. Through rigorous MATLAB/Simulink simulations and simulation validations on a lab-scale prototype, the converter's design not only meets but exceeds operational expectations, maintaining unity power factor and adhering to IEC61000-3-2 standards for total harmonic distortion, thereby highlighting its potential to significantly impact rural electrification and sustainable mobility.

articleTitle: Smart Assistance Device for the Visually Challenged: Integrating GPS Technology and Emergency Support Features with RTOS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: There are many problems faced by visually impaired people. Blinds find it very difficult to walk and also do many other small things. Their grief is huge. In this paper a solution is proposed to one of their problems in form of an innovative blind stick. The proposed model of this blind stick contains the smart system that is designed to send an emergency message with the message and location of the user to the guardian. The system contains the GPS and GSM modules which together accomplish this task. Visually impaired are guided by the micro controller which receives the emergency signal through a button. The push button is also connected to a buzzer that is loud enough to catch the attention of people around. Apart from these, the smart stick also contains sensors that are used for object detection. Hence, this model is beneficiary not only to the users but also to the guardians, as can be relieved to some extent. Finally, this paper focuses on developing an assistive technology for individuals with visual impairments. Utilizing an ESP32 micro controller and the FreeRTOS Real Time Operating System, the device leverages GPS technology and integrates emergency support features. Even FreeRTOS supports efficient Inter Process Communications like Mutex, Semaphores & message queues etc. This innovative tool aims to enhance user autonomy and security by providing essential navigation and safety functionalities.

articleTitle: Web Guardian: Harnessing Web Mining to Combat Online Terrorism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In recent years, terrorism has surged dramatically in specific regions, demanding immediate intervention to prevent its destructive impact on lives and property. Exploiting technological advancements, particularly the internet, terrorist groups utilize online platforms to spread propaganda, defame individuals, and recruit members for criminal activities. To effectively create a system, it is essential to use both web mining and data mining approaches to combat this danger. Web mining involves using several techniques for text mining to derive valuable insights from unorganized data. At the same time, data mining algorithms handle organized datasets, enhancing web mining's ability to navigate the intricacies of online material. However, the diverse data structures of websites pose challenges for unified algorithms. Web data mining assumes a critical role in detecting online terrorism spread, especially through the proliferation of phishing websites used for recruitment and coordination. By employing machine learning algorithms such as AdaBoost, SVM, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest, web data analysis can differentiate between legitimate and terrorist-associated sites by extracting features such as URL structure and domain age. Rigorous evaluation ensures the accuracy of these methods, enabling proactive measures like blocking identified terrorist activity sites. Through ongoing research and refinement, machine learning-driven web data mining emerges as a potent tool in combating the online dissemination of terrorist propaganda, reinforcing global security efforts.

articleTitle: Hardware Trojan Design and Analysis in FPGA an Introductory Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Hardware Trojan (HT) has been a rapidly developing area of interest in the hardware security world. They have impacted the Integrated Chips (IC) industry and increased the standards of testing and detection of malicious hardware. Although a wide range of literature has contributed to enhancing the design of hardware trojans and detection algorithms to identify trojans, scarce academic work is found in the area of hardware trojans in Field Programmable Gated Arrays (FPGAs). This project aims to understand the design and implementation of hardware trojans from an attacker's perspective, encompassing the technique of hardware trojan design, the potential attack vector, and the stealthiness of the hardware trojan. A state-machine-based hardware trojan is designed to attack the Universal Asynchronous Receive Transmitter UART. Firmware updates for a wide range of medical devices happen through serial communication or wireless transfer. Attacking the UART of these devices could corrupt the firmware of the device, which could corrupt the boot loader path, resulting in the malfunction of the device. This poses a very dangerous threat, especially in the medical device field, where less attention is given to security. The paper presents a demonstrative example of a hardware trojan attacking Booth's algorithm.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cyberbullying Detection Through Keyword Filtering: A Comparative Study of ML and DL Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Cyberbullying represents the use of online platforms like social media, gaming platforms, and similar platforms to harass a person, hurt a person, or threaten a person. In this study, keyword filtering is introduced to enhance cyberbullying detection. Various machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine, as well as a deep learning model Convolutional Neural Network, are implemented on original and keyword-labelled datasets. The performance of these models is compared using various evaluation metrics. Our findings demonstrate that the performance of models on the keyword-labeled dataset is significantly higher, with Logistic Regression achieving 98.24%, Random Forest at 99.77%, SVM at 99.67%, and CNN at 99.95% accuracy. This study highlights the effectiveness of keyword filtering features in enhancing the detection of cyberbullying, providing a robust approach to creating safer online environments.

articleTitle: Analysis of Skin Conductance Sensing Technique for Ulcerated Wound Healing Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This paper presents a system for assessing the ulcerated wound healing progress of the patient who suffers from medical condition such as diabetes mellitus and vascular disease. It helps the healthcare profession to easily diagnose the patient with non-healing ulcerated, chronic as well as acute wound. The proposed system is very economical, safe, non- invasive type and painless to the patients who suffer from non- healing wound. The usual method of monitoring the wound involves, dressing or opens the wound to analysis the healing progress which may not be convenient to the patients due to the psychological trauma. Therefore, the presented work effectively utilizes Galvanic skin response (GSR) sensor to sense the skin conductance value and Arduino UNO WiFi for the real-time data acquisition module to analyze the wound healing assessment. From the experimental results, it is observed that, the electrical properties of a human tissue are nearly same as in the gelatin mixture. The presented work is the initial phase of simple real-time data acquisition model. More experiments have to be conducted for the proper normalization of bioimpedance and skin conductance value of a healthy and wounded skin. Because, the performance of wound healing assessment depends on these factors. Further Thingspeak IOT platform is used to visualize the results in real-time environment.

articleTitle: Prediction of Chiller Thermal Characteristics in Radiant Cooling Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This study is intended to develop an artificial-neural-network (ANN)-based model that computes the necessary chiller thermal energy/heat transfer rate in a desiccant and sensible heat recovery wheel integrated vapor absorption-based radiant cooling system (RCS). Solar and natural gas were the main energy sources. The RCS was installed with a 4-floor corporate building of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4998 \ \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>. By applying the time-variant weather data, radiant and dedicated outdoor air system (DOAS) chiller capacities of the RCS may be pre-determined securely in a more convenient manner. During the development, the ANN structure was fed with input neurons containing solar irradiance, outdoor temperature, and moisture contents. These had statistical connection with the output neuron denoting radiant and DOAS chiller heat transfer rates. The entire ANN framework was optimized for the analysis and the parametric predictions. Results were studied using mean-squared error, correlation coefficient (R), and error histograms. For heat transfer rate predictions of radiant and DOAS chillers, R values were determined above 86% and 95%, respectively. Finally, histograms exhibited that for most of the samples, errors of 0.0025 and 0.03366 were involved with parametric predictions of radiant and DOAS chillers, respectively. Therefore, the presented ANN was proven to have the capability to be implemented in sustainable energy-based building designs.

articleTitle: An ML-based Resume Screening and Ranking System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In today's job market, resumes have flooded businesses, and the recruitment process has become an imposing task for companies. The traditional ways of resume screening are time-consuming and biased. To address these challenges, this research paper proposes a solution to automate this process through machine learning techniques. Based on existing research in this field, the aim is to improve the efficiency and accuracy of selecting candidates that are best suited for each job role without the use of complex techniques and provide equally good results. Existing methods involve the use of NLP, ML, and AI techniques to perform the screening process, each having its own advantages and disadvantages. Different ML models like SVM, Naive Bayes, and XGBoost have been explored and compared to find the most suitable and accurate approach. To improve accessibility and to implement a user-friendly system, a web application has also been created. On comparing the performance of these models using various performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, and F1 score, XGBoost is found to be the most suitable model with 0.89 AUC-ROC value and is used in the web application. As a novel approach, the candidates’ resumes are assigned scores based on the user's requirements and then ranked enabling the recruiter to shortlist suitable candidates for the job. This approach aims to simplify the resume screening process and revolutionize the hiring process.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Aerial Images Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a computer vision function that incorporates classifying each pixel in an image into a precise category or class. Unlike classification functions where the goal is to assign an exclusive label to the whole image, semantic segmentation furnishes a more detailed concern of the image by segmenting it into regions corresponding to distinct objects or structures. Similarly, this paper represents the model which scheme for utilizing the datasets of spatial resolutions also site for teaching a completely convolutional neural specification named the U-Net to finish the segmentation of aerial images. The dataset comprises 72 images captured by MBRSC (Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre) satellites, organized into six larger tiles. Each image is remarked with pixel-sharp semantic segmentation across six distinct classes: Vegetation, Water, Land (unpaved area), Road, Building and Unlabeled. Given the variability in image sizes, a crucial preprocessing step involves resizing the images to dimensions divisible by 256 and then extracting manageable patches. This ensures uniformity, enabling seamless processing and analysis. The accompanying mask images, initially provided in RGB format with HEX color codes, undergo conversion to standard RGB values. Subsequently, these RGB values are translated into integer labels, which are further transformed into a one-hot encoded format. This transformation is essential for facilitating the learning procedure of the deep learning model. The core of the project employs a U-Net architecture, a type of convolutional neural network (CNN) prominent for its effectiveness in image segmentation tasks. U-Net's structure, characterized by its symmetric contracting and expansive paths coupled with skip connections, allows for precise localization and classification of each pixel in the image. The network processes the preprocessed patches, generating segmented outputs that categorize each pixel according to the predefined classes. Post-segmentation, the predicted segmented images are converted back to their original RGB color representations. This step ensures that the segmented output aligns with the initial visual characteristics of the input data. The final phase of the project addresses the assembly of these segmented patches back into their respective larger tile structures. This involves merging the predicted tiles, taking care to minimize blending artifacts through smooth blending techniques. This approach ensures a seamless and coherent larger image, preserving the visual and spatial integrity of the original data.

articleTitle: An Omni-Directional Self driving Robot for Indoor Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Indoor surveillance stands as a critical measure for ensuring the safety and well-being of the elderly population, who often face various risks within their living spaces. To address this need effectively, this paper introduces a systematic approach to develop an omnidirectional self-driving robot tailored specifically for indoor surveillance tasks. The robot's design centers on the utilization of three omni wheels, providing holonomic motion and exceptional maneuverability within confined indoor environments. Leveraging the Robot Operating System (ROS) as the underlying framework and Jetson Nano as the development board, the integration of complex robotic systems is streamlined, ensuring seamless operation and versatility. With autonomous mobility capabilities, the robot is equipped to navigate indoor spaces autonomously, facilitating continuous monitoring through an integrated camera system. Key surveillance functionalities include detecting falls among the elderly and identifying potential intrusions. Moreover, the modular design of the robotic system enables the incorporation of additional surveillance features, further enhancing its utility and adaptability. Overall, this paper presents a robust hardware solution coupled with advanced functionalities, offering a comprehensive indoor surveillance system poised to address the diverse needs of residential environments.

articleTitle: A Survey on Machine and Deep Learning Approaches in Sign Language Recognition: Techniques and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Sign language is an essential communication medium for individuals with hearing impairments. It enables them to convey messages, disseminate knowledge, and transfer ideas within the deaf community. However, not everyone understands sign language, making it challenging for individuals with hearing impairments to communicate effectively with other common people. Sign Language Recognition (SLR) is vital for bridging the communication gap between persons with hearing loss and non-sign language speakers. This survey paper aims to explore Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques for recognition of sign languages. Investigate further research scope in this field.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Medical Diagnostics: Exploring Creativity in AI for Biomedical Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Biomedical image analysis plays a crucial role in the early and accurate diagnosis of diseases, significantly impacting patient outcomes. This study presents an innovative approach to biomedical image analysis by integrating machine learning techniques with a user-friendly web interface. The system takes input images uploaded through the web interface and processes them using advanced machine learning algorithms implemented in Python. The goal is to automate the detection of diseases from these images, enhancing the efficiency and precision of diagnosis. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a specialized class of deep learning models designed for image analysis, are employed to learn and characterize disease-specific patterns. The proposed approach is evaluated using diverse biomedical images encompassing various diseases and conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the system's effectiveness, achieving high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity in disease detection. Integrating machine learning with a web interface simplifies the diagnostic process and enables remote consultations, making healthcare services more accessible and timelier. In conclusion, this study presents a robust framework for automated biomedical image analysis, demonstrating the potential of machine learning and web technologies in revolutionizing healthcare diagnostics. The system's accuracy and user-friendly interface make it a valuable tool for healthcare professionals, contributing to early disease detection and improved patient care.

articleTitle: Machine Learning vs. Deep Learning for Personalized Medicine Recommendations: A Sentiment Analysis Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of sentiment analysis algorithms, which includes Support Vector Machines (SVM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Simple Neural Network, and Naive Bayes Utilizing a variety of datasets from social media sentiments and product reviews, the study thoroughly evaluates both the computational complexities and practical performance of these methods. Through comprehensive experiments and analysis of metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, the study reveals the distinct effectiveness of each algorithm for different sentiment analysis tasks. The findings highlights the strengths and limitations of eachapproach, offering valuable insights for practitioners seeking to navigate the landscape of sentiment analysis techniques. By contributing towards the ongoing discourse on advancing sentiment analysis in the context of big data and computational linguistics, this study aims to inform algorithm selection and promote advancements in NLP research.

articleTitle: Deep Fake Detection using Transfer Learning: A Comparative study of Multiple Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: With the proliferation of sophisticated AI techniques, the creation and dissemination of deep fake images and videos have emerged as a pressing concern in today's digital landscape. Deep fake technology employs advanced machine learning algorithms to manipulate or synthesize realistic-looking media, often with malicious intent. This study evaluates the effectiveness of various pre-trained deep learning models using transfer learning for detecting deep fake images on the Face Forensics++ dataset. The models considered include MobileN etV2, ResN et50, Inception V3, EfficientN et, Xception, NASNetMobile, and a Custom CNN. Accuracies obtained from these models are compared to assess their performance in distinguishing between real and fake images. With the highest performance in MobileNetV2 with 89% followed by ResNet50 with 83 % and other models.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Agriculture Farm Monitoring System and Development of Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Throughout history, agriculture or farming has played a vital role in human civilization by providing people's fundamental necessities and significant contributions to a country's economy. Although small-scale smart farming has started in a few nations, it has yet to be adopted scientifically globally. The rapid growth of the world population along with urbanization has rendered modern agriculture increasingly essential day by day. Towards multi-domain modernization, the Internet of Things (IoT) technology is a developing paradigm that aims to link many smart physical parameters in smart agriculture. In this paper, an IoT-based smart agricultural farm monitoring system prototype has been proposed which has been designed considering different environmental parameters. Additionally, image processing-based plant disease detection model has been developed in two different methods. The system incorporates various sensors, actuators, and a microcontroller to monitor and control temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and rainfall. It also includes a water pump motor for automated irrigation where a Wi-Fi module allows remote monitoring and controlled by a developed smartphone app. To validate, the proposed hardware model was simulated using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. There have been notable outcomes observed on temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and other monitoring parameters data reading from LCD. Also, deep learning-based image processing algorithm has been proposed using Feature extraction and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods and achieved a high accuracy of about 96%-98% in plant disease detection. The overall proposed system offers improved resource utilization and smart agricultural practices for expanded functionalities and long-term sustainability to ensure food security for the growing population.

articleTitle: Locating Patient Health Data Theft Using Gradient Boosting with Hybrid Microwave Transmission-Based Wearable Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The research article addresses the intersection of healthcare monitoring and crime prevention via wearable devices in hospital settings. It proposes a system leveraging blockchain, decision-making algorithms, and wireless communication, particularly IoT and gradient-boosting approaches. Existing health care monitoring lacks real-time intervention capabilities, and conventional crime prevention methods are often reactive rather than proactive. The revolutionary combination of gradient boosting and hybrid microwave transmission-based wearable devices is the ultimate solution to combat patient health data theft. With this cutting-edge technology, this research can confidently detect and prevent unauthorised access to sensitive healthcare information, ensuring the safety and privacy of patients. The proposed system ensures continuous health monitoring and prompt interventions while enhancing crime prevention through mobile data analysis. Blockchain and decision-making algorithms are integrated to securely store patient data and enable authorised personnel access for review. IoT and gradient-boosting algorithms facilitate real-time health monitoring and accurate prediction of crime-related patterns through mobile data analysis. The proposed gradient boosting algorithm has an RMSE of 0.105 and an MAE of 0.010, suggesting great prediction accuracy. With a V AF score of 96% and an R-squared score of 0.94, it captures data variability while demonstrating predictive solid power. This comprehensive strategy utilises cutting-edge technology to enhance healthcare monitoring via wearable devices, contribute to crime prevention, and address crucial concerns in healthcare and public safety.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Off-Grid Solar Power System, Integrating MPPT and Smart Battery Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The MPPT algorithm described in this research uses the perturb and observe (P&O) approach to maximize power output for a Smart Battery Management System (SBMS). The system produces power that is clean and dependable with an astounding 85% inverter efficiency and a low Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of less than 2.91 %. It also has a short repayment period 6 years. With two user-specific batteries (Battery 1 and Battery 2) and a central battery (via the SBMS), the design effectively controls reliability and a continuous energy supply. This creative method emphasizes how dedicated the system is to provide cost-effective and environmentally friendly energy solutions. Emphasizing dependability and continuous energy supply, the design incorporates a Smart Battery Management System (SBMS) to efficiently manage two user-specific batteries (Battery 1 and Battery 2) alongside a central battery. Utilizing MPPT controllers for solar panel optimization, surplus energy is seamlessly redirected to the central battery when user batteries are fully charged, ensuring uninterrupted power availability. The emphasis on cost-effectiveness and flexible technology positions this modern off-grid solar power system as a practical and economical solution, addressing energy poverty in rural areas while promoting environmental sustainability through optimized hardware performance.

articleTitle: Augmented GAN: Advancing Generative Adversarial Networks Through Enhanced Discriminator Training and Generator Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: General Adversarial Networks (GANs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generating reliable and transformative synthetic data in areas such as image generation, image and text synthesis, and data augmentation. This paper presents a comprehensive guide to building a Generative Adversarial Neural Network using TensorFlow and Python. Through our research on this topic, we delve into the implementation details, providing step-by-step instructions for constructing both the generator and discriminator networks using TensorFlow, a popular deep-learning framework. Furthermore, we explore techniques for optimizing GAN performance, including architectural modifications, loss function selection, and training strategies. We demonstrate how to train a GAN on real-world datasets through practical examples, showcasing its capability to generate high-quality synthetic samples that closely resemble the training data distribution. In this paper, we aim to match fashion products such as clothing and accessories using GAN. This paper also focuses on improving the robustness and generalization of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, such as image classification and product recommendation. By combining image results with GANs and incorporating these artificial data into the training process, we aim to improve the performance of CNN models in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Survey of Ankylosing Spondylitis for Biomedical Imaging with Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammat ory disease that affects the axial spine and peripheral joints, manifesting through symptoms such as spinal stiffness, back pain, and joint involvement. Medical imaging, particularly X-rays and MRIs, is essential for diagnosing AS and monitoring its progression. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning techniques, have significantly enhanced AS diagnosis by enabling the automated analysis of medical images to identify subtle patterns and markers indicative of the disease. This paper introduces an innovative framework that integrates deep learning with Explainable AI (XAI) techniques to improve the diagnostic process for AS. Our deep learning model, trained on an extensive dataset of MRI scans, demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in detecting AS. Nevertheless, the inherent complexity of deep learning models, often described as “black box” models, raises concerns about their interpretability and transparency in clinical decision-making. To address these challenges, we incorporate XAI methods such as Grad-CAM and LIME, which provide visual and feature-based explanations of the model's predictions. These techniques enhance the interpretability of the model, allowing clinicians to understand and trust AI-driven decisions. The novelty of our approach lies in the seamless integration of XAI methods with deep learning for AS diagnosis, which not only improves diagnostic accuracy but also ensures compliance with ethical and legal standards in healthcare. Continued research and collaboration between AI experts and healthcare professionals are crucial to fully realizing the potential of deep learning and XAI in AS diagnosis and to ultimately enhance patient care.

articleTitle: FinSecure: Utilizing IoT Sensors for Formaldehyde Detection and Fish Freshness Detection for Enhancing Safety in Fish Consumption Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The global food supply heavily relies on fisheries, highlighting the crucial importance of ensuring the safety of fish products. However, the widespread application of antibiotics and the existence of compounds such as formaldehyde present significant hazards to both human consumers and the underwater ecosystem. These risks are compounded by processes like bio-magnification, further emphasizing the need for vigilant monitoring and regulation. This project presents a comprehensive approach to fisheries management and food safety monitoring through the integration of advanced machine learning, deep learning techniques and IoT sensor technology. The overall objective is to develop a model that can determine whether the given sample Fish Species is safe or unsafe for human consumption, by considering parameters: Fish Freshness Detection, using a HCHO Sensor to determine the Formaldehyde levels in the given Fish and finally using these parameters to determine whether the fish can be consumed or not. For the Fish Freshness Detection, utilizing Transfer Learning (pre-trained MobileNetV2 model), the system achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.02%. Thus, integrating all these models, determine whether the supplied fish is safe for consumption or not. By integrating these functionalities, the system contributes to proactive fisheries and food safety monitoring and protection. The holistic approach of this project, combining accurate positions the developed model and IoT application as valuable assets for sustainable aquaculture practices and the preservation of aquatic ecosystems. The project's outcomes contribute to the advancement of several interdisciplinary domains such as machine learning, and fisheries management, laying the groundwork for continued innovation in this interdisciplinary domain.

articleTitle: Reviewing Cheating and Detection Techniques in Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games: A Systematic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In recent years, despite the shift of massively multiplayer online role-playing games (MMORPGs) from PC to mobile platforms, fraudulent and illegal activities persist within the online gaming market. These issues hinder players’ immersion and enjoyment of the game, potentially leading to their disengagement from the gaming community, thereby negatively impacting the industry as a whole. This systematic review offers an in-depth examination of existing studies concerning cheating behaviors, countermeasures, and detection methods in MMORPGs. Our focus is on understanding the underlying reasons for cheating behavior within the structural framework of state-full game servers and exploring the fundamental mechanisms of online gaming, particularly within the context of MMORPGs. Through extensive literature research, we have organized and categorized countermeasures and detection methods systematically. The findings of this review contribute to a deeper understanding of effective strategies for managing and combating cheating behaviors within MMORPGs.

articleTitle: Predicting Optimal Solar Cell Design for Enhanced Degradation Resistance based on Environmental Conditions Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: This research aims to develop a machine learning based predictive model to optimize the selection of solar cell materials for perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on environmental conditions. We explore how machine learning models can improve the efficiency and longevity of PSCs. We consider the environmental condition such as existence of O2, humidity, stored conditions and desired efficiency of the PSC to be the feature space for our predictive machine learning model. After evaluating some renowned machine learning algorithms for our predictive model, the Decision Tree Regression outperforms other algorithms. Our machine learning algorithm is designed to forecast an optimized architecture for PSC capable of enduring specific environmental conditions, ensuring a maximum tenure before experiencing an 80% drop in initial efficiency. By integrating machine learning techniques into our research is to improve the efficiency and lifespan of solar energy systems, thereby advancing sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Empowering Women: A Creative Approach to Integrated Safety with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: An extensive platform created to provide women with a sense of security and empowerment in their everyday lives is the Integrated Women's Safety Application. Users can use apps with assurance that their data is safe thanks to secure login functionality. The software offers users messaging warnings alerting them to potential hazards in their neighbourhood, as well as a panic button for emergency assistance in case of an emergency. In addition to offering directions, Route Navigation also indicates the locations of neighbouring police stations for an extra layer of security. A smooth and effective method for requesting assistance and recording hazardous circumstances is created by enabling users to report issues straight from the app. In addition, the heatmap visualization tool helps users make educated judgments about their travels by providing a visual depiction of safety ratings in various locations. The Integrated Women's Safety Application attempts to equip women with the tools to navigate the world confidently and safely by combining these essential aspects into a single platform.

Author Keywords: safe and secure environment for women

articleTitle: An Efficient AI Based System for the Detection of Diabetic Maculopathy Using Colour Fundus Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
