abstract: Among people with diabetes, diabetic maculopathy, a dangerous consequence of diabetic retinopathy is the primary cause of visual impairment. Effective treatment and management depend on early and precise identification. In this research, datasets from Kaggle, DRIVE, CHASE, STARE and DIARETDB1 is employed and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based method is used for recognizing the presence of diabetic maculopathy. Multiple convolutional layers make up the model architecture, which is then followed by pooling and fully connected layers. A SoftMax method is then used to categorize the data and is extensively tuned for hyperparameters. By incorporating transfer learning from pre-trained models, the performance is further improved and a significant reduction in training period and processing resources is required. Using a variety of datasets guarantees a thorough assessment of the model, improving its dependability and generalizability. The model's capacity to retain excellent performance across several data sources is confirmed by independent testing and cross-validation on each dataset. By facilitating prompt medical intervention, the suggested CNN model might possibly improve patient outcomes by aiding in the early detection of diabetic maculopathy. With a sensitivity of 90%, specificity of 98%, precision of 97.8%, accuracy of 94%, and F1 score of 93.8%, our model performed well. These measurements highlight the promise of deep learning approaches in improving medical imaging diagnostics by demonstrating the model's resilience and efficacy in diagnosing diabetic maculopathy. Accuracy obtained using completed Local Binary Pattern (CLBP) and Deep Learning-Based Framework for Automatic Diabetic Retinopathy Detection is found to be 90% and 91 %, whereas the proposed method offers an accuracy of 94% which is better and optimum.

articleTitle: Navigating the AI Landscape: A Comparative Study of Models, Applications, and Emerging Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In today's technology world, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has grown omnipresent, transforming industries and affecting many facets of our everyday lives. Given the abundance of AI models in many categories, it is critical to comprehend their advantages, disadvantages, and uses in order to make well-informed decisions and progress the field. NLP, Computer Vision, Speech Recognition, Robotics, Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, Deep Learning models, Reinforcement Learning, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Expert Systems, Au- tonomous Vehicles, Recommendation Systems, and Predictive Analytics are just a few of the categories that this paper compares and reviews in depth. We assess each model's performance, scalability, and appropriateness for various applications through a methodical examination. By combining extant research with practical examples, we illustrate the state of AI technologies now and offer predictions for their future development. The goal of this assessment is to help experts in the industry, researchers, and practitioners navigate the intricate AI ecosystem and realize AI's full potential for the good of society.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic based Man-in-the-Middle Attack Detection Scheme in Advanced Metering Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Man-in-the-middle attack in advanced metering infrastructure allows intruders to monitor and manipulate communications among legitimate users, which poses a crucial threat to network security. The traditional signature based intrusion detection schemes involves large number of rules that imposes computational complexity on resource constraint devices. Further, the conventional intrusion detection schemes are used for binary classification where severity of the threat based solutions cannot be achieved. To evade this, fuzzy logic based intrusion detection scheme that incorporates various subnets of internet protocol addressing and mac addresses as input and decision on the severity of threat as output. The attack is emulated using Ettercap and the packet information is captured using Wireshark. The data is pre-processed and the input term sets with predefined ranges and membership functions are derived. The fuzzy rules are framed to identify the vulnerability level based on the fuzzy sets assigned to the internet protocol and media access control addresses. The proposed fuzzy based intrusion detection scheme is implemented in Python. The results exhibit that the proposed fuzzy based scheme exhibits its efficiency.

articleTitle: 3DSC2-UNet: Advancing Breast Cancer Segmentation Techniques Using the 3D Skipped Convolution Capsule-UNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) persists as a substantial global health hurdle, demanding ongoing progress in the realms of detection, diagnosis, and therapeutic approaches. This thorough examination delves into cutting-edge technologies and methodologies that have surfaced in the quest for enhanced results in BC management. Yet, investigations employing solitary imaging modalities have showcased restricted clinical effectiveness owing to their relatively diminished diagnostic precision and dependability when compared to multimodal systems. As a result, our aim is to create a 3D Skipped Convolution Capsule UNet designed for the segmentation of breast tumors, employing both mammogram and ultrasound imaging modalities. For the integration of these modalities, we utilize the Dynamic Fusion Net (DF-Net), incorporating two modules named the Molecular-Level Aligner Module and Biphasic Sequential Integration Module (BSInU). The process of segmentation takes place within our innovative framework, 3DSC2-UNet, encompassing four primary elements: (a) Graphical feature extraction, (b) Convolutional Capsule (ConvCaps) encoder module, (c) Synaptic skip connection, and (d) Convolutional decoder (Conv Decoder). The overall accuracy attained is 99.97%, accompanied by a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.89 and an Average Surface Distance (ASD) of 2.5mm across the mammogram dataset. Moreover, the precision stands at 99.65%, accompanied by a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.88 and an Average Surface Distance (ASD) of 2.4mm across the ultrasound dataset. The suggested 3DSC2-UNet, harnessing both mammogram and ultrasound, showcases exceptional performance in accuracy, ASD, and DSC metrics. This model holds the capability to diminish unwarranted biopsy procedures, thereby advancing its prospects for clinical implementation.

articleTitle: Heart Attack Prediction Using Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Heart attacks are a leading cause of death worldwide, making it a necessity to develop accurate prediction systems for timely intervention and prevention. This paper addresses the challenge of heart attack prediction through ensemble learning methodologies. Previous research has primarily focused on individual machine learning algorithms, often overlooking the potential of ensemble techniques to improve predictive accuracy. In this study, we employed a dataset comprising various clinical features and medical indicators. After preprocessing steps such as encoding categorical variables, scaling, and balancing data using SMOTE, we explored multiple machine learning models, including logistic regression, SVM, KNN, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting, and artificial neural networks. Additionally, feature selection techniques and hyperparameter optimization were utilized to enhance model performance. Finally, we employed ensemble learning, specifically Stacking, to combine the strengths of individual models, resulting in a higher predictive accuracy of 93%. The results demonstrate the high efficiency of ensemble learning in heart attack prediction, showcasing a significant improvement over individual models.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Skin Disease Classification: A Study of Transfer Learning Strategies for Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Skin diseases are a common health concern globally, requiring accurate diagnosis and treatment. Various techniques, including medication, topical treatments, phototherapy, and surgery, are employed for their cure. The detection of skin diseases has evolved significantly, with advancements in AI Technologies like image processing, machine learning, and deep learning. Image processing techniques extract meaningful features from images, while ML and DL algorithms classify diseases based on these features. In this work, we utilize a dataset of 23 classes, each containing 192 training images and 20 testing images. The dataset used here is the class-balanced dataset. We employ image processing techniques to enhance the dataset, followed by classification using DL models such as VGG19 and ResNet50. Our models achieve 83.69% and 82.82% accuracy, demonstrating their efficacy for classifying the skin disease images. This study contributes to the advancement of automation work of skin disease classification for diagnosis and treatment planning.

articleTitle: Image-Based Plant Leaf Disease Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Abstract-Deep learning (DL) has recently gained a wide attention in detection of plant leaf diseases. However, the effectiveness of DL depends on the vast amount of data to derive the meaningful patterns which is crucial for accurate detection. This led to the appreciation of pretrained models, which are trained on large data for improved detection despite limited data in the required domain. This paper presents an ensemble-based DL model for detecting diseases in cucumber plant leaves. The proposed ensemble learning framework includes Resnet V50, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNet-B0 as the pretrained models which aggregate the output of these models by weighted ensemble averaging. Data augmentation and Hyperparameter tunings were performed to increase the model generalization and capability. The proposed ensemble approach was validated on Cucumber Disease Recognition Dataset and achieved an accuracy of 99.351%, precision of 99.363% and F1 Score of 99.352% that outperforms the underlying learning framework. Additionally, to provide more insights into the extent of a model to predict each class, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is employed that produces heat maps highlighting the regions which contributed most to the prediction.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transparency: AI Applications for Detecting Cheating and Predicting Player Attrition in Online Gaming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The online gaming industry, a thriving multibillion-dollar sector with a vast global audience, has greatly benefited from the integration of AI technology. However, the widespread adoption of black-box AI models in gaming systems has raised concerns regarding their lack of transparency and accountability. In this article, we address this issue by introducing Explainable AI (XAI) concepts tailored to online gaming environments. We propose a GXAI (Game Explainable AI) workflow that combines the rich insights from multiview data sources with the transparent nature of multiview black-box models. Our approach encompasses four specific classifiers and explainers, each offering unique perspectives: character portrait view, behavior sequence view, client image view, and social graph view. Through experiments conducted on real-world datasets, focusing on cheating detection and player churn prediction, we demonstrate the accuracy of our classification methods and the coherence of our explanations.

articleTitle: POS Tagging Using Hidden Markov Models in Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In this paper, we thoroughly examine the fundamental part which is Parts-Of-Speech (POS) Tagging of Natural Language Processing (NLP), especially. Our examination revolves around Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) usage to face up to this crucial element of language comprehension. Starting with the fundamental principles of the NLP, we go through its history after that, and we explore the inner workings of the N-gram Models and the Markov Models with a more detailed view finally in Hidden Markov Models. We meticulously uncover approaches used in POS Tagging preparation, so that we can get down to the in-depth methodological part of the journey. The intricate workings of Viterbi Algorithm and Maximum Entropy Markov Models will be clarified in the methodology section as they are keystone in our POS Tagging exploits. By performing highly standardized experimentation, we check the competence of HMMs in POS tagging, separately with CRFs (Conditional Random Fields). Ultimately, the report is a comprehensive description of the use of Hidden Markov Models in POS Tagging, that presents the applications, theoretical and practical bases, and the implications in the area of natural language understanding.

articleTitle: SQL Injection Detection Using Optimized Recurrent Neural Network Integrated with N-Gram: A Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: SQL injection is a serious security issue that can lead to data breaches and identity theft. Detecting SQL injection attempts in real time is important to prevent attacks and identify vulnerabilities. The performance of Particle Swarm Optimizer., Ant Colony Optimizer., and Artificial Bee Colony optimizer in training Recurrent Neural Networks for SQL detection using N-gram analysis is compared. The inclusion of N-gram analysis significantly improves the RNN-based model's performance., making it a promising solution for detecting SQL injection attacks in real-world web applications.

articleTitle: Metal Surface Defect Detection Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Metal defect detection plays a crucial role in ensuring the quality and safety of industrial manufacturing processes. Traditional methods of defect detection often rely on manual inspection, which can be time-consuming and prone to human error. In recent years, the application of deep learning techniques, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has shown promising results in automating defect detection tasks. This research explores the effectiveness of using CNN architectures, specifically InceptionNet, ResNet34, and VGG16, for automated metal defect detection. The study involves training and evaluating these models on a dataset of metal surface images containing various types of defects. The performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are analysed to assess the robustness and efficacy of each model in defect classification. Additionally, the research investigates the impact of transfer learning by fine-tuning pre-trained CNN models on the defect detection task. The experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of deep CNNs compared to traditional methods, highlighting the potential of these techniques for real-world applications in industrial quality control and inspection.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Energy in Wireless Sensor Network-Based IOT Application Using CR-MSGT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The monitoring of physical conditions in a variety of contexts is greatly aided by Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Regarding energy consumption and network performance, WSNs depend on efficient routing methods for data transfer. By comparing the CR-MSGT approach's performance to other routing protocols, this study assesses the energy efficiency of WSNs. Proactive, reactive, and hybrid protocols are among the categories of routing protocols that are examined, depending on how they operate and the applications for which they are intended. Together with data-centric, hierarchical, and location-based techniques, the research also examines direct communication, flat, and clustering protocols. Findings point to the potential of CR-MSGT for increasing network scalability and optimizing energy use. Research findings help to improve WSN performance in Internet of Things applications.

articleTitle: Stock Recommendation System for Better Investment Plan
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In the volatile landscape of financial markets, making well-informed decisions for intraday trading and long-term investment necessitates an integrated analysis of real-time stock data and the contextual information provided by news articles. This paper presents an innovative stock recommendation system that leverages advanced Machine Learning (ML) techniques and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to deliver timely, data-driven recommendations by assessing both risk and profit potential. Our system employs ML algorithms to process live stock price, trading volume, and technical indicators, enabling real-time assessment of a stock's performance. Developing a stock recommendation system is a challenging undertaking that frequently calls for a multidisciplinary team with experience in data science, machine learning, and finance. Simultaneously, it harnesses NLP models to extract sentiment and contextual information from news articles, providing insights into market sentiment and potential impact on stock behavior. By merging these two streams of data, our system offers a comprehensive view of stock's dynamics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Elderly Care Through Telehealth Monitoring System Utilizing xDNN Model: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The ageing population poses an increasing challenge to healthcare systems around the world, necessitating creative solutions to assure appropriate care for the elderly. This abstract investigates the importance of using Telehealth Monitoring Systems integrated with Explainable Deep Neural Network (xDNN) models to address the special healthcare demands of the older population. By incorporating xDNN models into Telehealth Monitoring Systems, real-time health data may be analyzed more accurately, allowing for early diagnosis of health conditions, personalized therapies, and predictive analytics. Telehealth technologies provide promising alternatives for remotely delivering healthcare services, particularly to seniors with mobility constraints or who live in remote places. This abstract covers the review of such a system, including improved quality of life for elderly people, empowerment and independence, reduced healthcare inequities.

articleTitle: Contactless Attendance Management System Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Introducing an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Con-tactless Attendance Management System. Conventional atten-dance techniques are laborious and prone to mistakes. By using facial recognition technology, the system eliminates the need for human operations by automating the marking of attendance. Ac-curate student identification is made possible without interfering with classroom activities through the use of real-time picture capture and data comparison with stored information. Using an OpenCV library and a Logitech C270 HD Webcam, the system is based on a Raspberry Pi platform and exhibits effective face detection and recognition capabilities. The system's usefulness in a range of lighting settings and positions is demonstrated by the experimental findings. This technology improves teaching-learning while lowering administrative expenses by providing a smooth and effective substitute for traditional attendance methods. Potential future developments might concentrate on maximizing system scalability and accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimization of Traffic System using Adaptive Response First Come First Serve
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: In this period of urbanization and adding vehicular traffic, the optimization of business operation systems is consummate to insure both the effectiveness of transportation networks and the safety of commuters. This exploration paper explores the operation of deep literacy ways to revise the field of business operation. By employing the power of deep learning, sensors and timers, our study aims to develop innovative results that ameliorate the delicacy, rigidity, and real- time responsiveness of business control systems. The primary focus of this exploration is to design a comprehensive deep literacy-grounded business operation system that incorporates colorful data sources. By assaying vast quantities of miscellaneous data, the system will acclimatize to dynamic business conditions and offer real- time perceptivity for effective business inflow operation, accident discovery, and traffic relief. The exploration will also explore the integration of machine literacy algorithms for intelligent business signal control, prioritizing green light allocation grounded on real- time demand and business viscosity. The proposed deep literacy result aims to significantly reduce business traffic, minimize trip times, and enhance overall road safety by furnishing optimized business operation strategies. The exploration will concentrate on the practical perpetration of the system in real- world business scripts, with the eventuality to gauge and acclimatize to colorful civic surroundings. This exploration bid seeks to lay the foundation for a future in which business systems seamlessly acclimatize to evolving business patterns, creating safer, more effective transportation networks, and contributing to a sustainable and intelligent civic ecosystem. The proposed dynamic signal control logic is 83.33 % more efficient in utilizing green time compared to the traditional fixed-time system. Estimated reduction in wasted green time is 25%.

articleTitle: Optimized Fabric Imperfection Detection via Image Analysis and Isolation Forest Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Fabric defect detection plays a crucial role in ensuring the quality of textile products. Traditional methods often rely on manual inspection, which is time-consuming and prone to human error. In this research, a novel method for fabric defect detection based on machine learning technique for anomaly detection the Isolation Forest algorithm is presented. The Isolation Forest algorithm builds a random forest of isolation trees to take advantage of the idea of isolating anomalies in a dataset. For the purpose of identifying fabric defects, every fabric sample is represented by a collection of features, including structural attributes, colour, and texture. By separating the majority of non-defective samples from the defective fabric samples, the Isolation Forest algorithm effectively finds the defective fabric samples. Based on the Standard Fabric Defect, our model also obtains a true positive rate value of 0.95 without generating any false alarms on our dataset.

Author Keywords: BIRCH (balanced iterative reducing and clustering using hierarchies) Algorithm

articleTitle: A Smart Vehicle Alert System with Intelligent Vehicle Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Road safety is a critical concern worldwide, with millions of lives lost and countless injuries sustained in traffic accidents annually. To address this pressing issue, a costeffective and reliable solution is proposed for enhancing road safety. The system leverages affordable sensors, wireless communication, and data analytics to combine accident detection, driver drowsiness monitoring, and real-time vehicle tracking. An accelerometer is utilized to detect collisions, an eye blink sensor to monitor driver drowsiness, and GPS for precise vehicle tracking. Upon accident detection or driver drowsiness, the system sends alerts via SMS and a mobile app, providing real-time location information. The microcontroller processes sensor data and controls communication modules, prioritizing critical events. Extensive testing demonstrates high accuracy in accident detection (95% in cities, 70% in rural areas), driver drowsiness detection (96<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), and unauthorized access detection (97%). The system also excels in detecting accidents in parking mode (95%) and offers a battery backup of 1–2 days. Comparative analysis highlights the system's superiority in terms of accuracy, comprehensive features, and integration of multiple safety aspects. The proposed system's impact extends beyond individual vehicles, offering opportunities for innovation, economic growth, and sustainable transportation. With ongoing improvements and consideration of ethical and societal factors, this system has the potential to revolutionize vehicle safety and contribute to a safer, smarter transportation ecosystem.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Dynamic Microservices Composition: Harnessing the Power of the PMCE Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: The microservices architectural strategy empowers organizations to develop software comprised of small, independent services that communicate via well-defined Application Pro-gramming Interfaces (APIs). These services, collectively forming a microservices architecture (MSA), boast high maintainability, loose coupling, and autonomous deployment capabilities. This architectural paradigm fosters scalability and facilitates the integration of agile requirements or new features. Each service is designed to address specific business functionalities. However managing the logic and execution sequence of multiple microservices within an MSA can be challenging. Orchestration and communication between these services require careful coor-dination. Determining the appropriate size and functionality of each microservice to meet business needs is also a complex task, despite the scalability and flexibility benefits it offers. Recognizing these challenges there are many industry orchestration engines for seamless microservices composition. These are robust and secure but while adhering to these engines is a big hurdles for organisations as the Complexity, scalability limitations, vendor lock-in, limited customization, and high costs are drawbacks of these orchestration engines. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for dynamic microservices composition using the Probabilistic Markov Chain Engine (PMCE) framework. This innovative method leverages the power of Markov Chains to dynamically select and orchestrate microservices based on his-torical performance, reliability, and transition probabilities. By continuously adapting to real-time data, the PMCE framework enhances system efficiency, resilience, and responsiveness. Our approach significantly improves service composition in complex, distributed environments, ensuring optimal performance and seamless user experiences. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the PMCE framework in various scenarios, show-casing its potential as a robust solution for modern microservices architecture.

articleTitle: Improving Wart Treatment Efficacy Prediction with Immunotherapy and Cryotherapy Using SVM, RF, CVM, k-NN, MLP, and BLR Algorithms in Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Warts, characterized by small, rough, benign tumors induced by human papillomavirus (HPV), pose a challenge in treatment prediction due to variations in patient response and disease characteristics. While a machine learning-based expert prediction system and associated rules have been proposed, their success remains unsatisfactory and lacks interpretability for medical professionals. In this study, we employ a decision tree-based approach to delineate rules for predicting wart treatment success. Our findings reveal success rates ranging from 90% to 95% across different treatment methods, surpassing previous reports. Additionally, the decision tree rules generated can be converted into visual representations, enabling intuitive interpretation of treatment success rates in relation to patient age and disease duration. This method offers a straightforward and more precise interpretation of rules for medical experts, facilitating the prediction of treatment success as a percentage.

articleTitle: EXTENSION FOR HANDWRITTEN CHARACTER RECOGNITION USING RNN-GRU ALGORITHM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Recognizing handwritten characters is a complex task in pattern recognition and computer vision, demanding advanced techniques to enable computers to discern and transform handwritten or printed characters into a digital format. The integration of the GRU algorithm within the RNN-CNN hybrid methodology marks a significant advancement in handwritten character recognition. By transitioning from a character-by-character to a line-by-line recognition approach, the system aims to improve the conversion of handwritten text into digital formats. GRU enhances context awareness by predicting subsequent letters in incomplete words, thereby facilitating more accurate recognition. Leveraging the IAM dataset not only provides ample training data but also aids in error detection and correction, enhancing the overall accuracy and reliability of the system. This innovative approach underscores a commitment to advancing OCR capabilities beyond isolated characters and words, toward more comprehensive and context-aware text recognition, thereby paving the way for more effective digitization of handwritten documents.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Classification using Continuous Wavelet Transform Scalogram and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Automated classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is pivotal for timely and accurate diagnosis of cardiac abnormalities. In this work weintroduces a new method for classifying electrocardiogram (ECG) signals by merging signal processing and deep learning techniques. We utilize Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) to convert one-dimensional ECG signals into scalogram images, capturing both temporal and frequency details. By employing transfer learning, we fine-tune a pre-trained AlexNet Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to categorize ECG signals into three types: arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, and normal sinus rhythm. We extensively compare our method with existing approaches, demonstrating its superior performance with an accuracy of 96%. The hierarchical structure of AlexNet enables the extraction of intricate features from ECG signals, surpassing other models that suffer from shallow architectures and reliance on manual feature engineering. Our approach not only improves automated ECG analysis but also holds promise for enhancing clinical diagnosis and management of cardiovascular conditions.

articleTitle: Interactive Learning with AlphAR: A Symbol-Recognition Aid for Dyslexic Children Through Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Dyslexia is a neurological condition that affects a person's ability to read, write, and spell. It is characterized by difficulties in processing phonological information, leading to challenges in acquiring fluent and accurate reading skills. Early assistance fosters a positive learning trajectory, enhancing the overall well-being and confidence of dyslexic individuals. AlphAR is an innovative augmented reality (AR) web system specifically tailored to address the challenges of symbol recognition in dyslexic children, developed using cutting-edge A-Frame and AR.js technologies. It harnesses marker-based AR to create an immersive learning environment. The novelty lies in its seamless integration of marker patterns with corresponding 3D models, facilitating interactive learning experiences for children aged 5 to 10. Through intuitive user interface elements and audio cues, AlphAR enhances engagement and promotes auditory learning. Ethical design principles ensure inclusivity and user-friendliness, prioritizing participant comfort and engagement. Users interact with the system through intuitive gestures, such as flipping down and left, further enhancing skill development. The iterative nature of AlphAR allows for adaptability to individual learning paces, fostering a positive and inclusive experimental environment. To validate AlphAR's effectiveness, we will benchmark it against established AR interventions like LitAR, AHA System and many others.

articleTitle: Semantic Wireless Communications: Unveiling the Next Frontier in Intelligent Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Semantic communication, a multidisciplinary field, transforms communication technology by integrating semantic understanding and improving information flow efficiency. This study surveys various aspects of semantic communication to explore its multiple facets. This paper delves into the fundamental concepts of semantics in communication, emphasizing the importance of meaning extraction and interpretation. In this approach, The semantic problem focuses on the precision of conveying meaning, ensuring accurate information transmission while maintaining its original semantic relevance. This work presents an overview, and advancement to date, as well as identifies research issues and challenges in semantic communication. The paper, in principle, addresses the overview, technical issues, systems, and innovative technologies associated with semantic communication. The paper finally presents recommendations and future trends associated with this emerging future communication system. This provides a valuable reference and new avenues for future research in this direction.

articleTitle: Advancing Video Summarization Using Language-Based Attention Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Video summarization is a process geared towards condensing lengthy videos into concise summaries, facilitating efficient browsing and context understanding. Traditionally, supervised learning-based approaches have been introduced to capture significant content within video, and steer the summarization task by leveraging continuous frame-level data, though they suffer from semantic gaps between what is depicted visually and what is contextually meaningful, offer limited generality and limited generalization, and rely heavily on human-curated summaries for training. In response to these gaps, a transformer- based framework is proposed, as a novel direction, primarily built on a Cross-Attention Transformer (CAT), which uses CLIP ViT-B/32 for visual or frame features and Clip for caption features. Further, we introduced a language-guided multimodal transformer to twofold support, firstly to assess the importance of each video relative to one another in an automatically generated and comprehensive video caption, and secondly, to compare the similarity score of each frame with caption tokens to get the gist of the video. Through extensive evaluations of standard video summarization datasets (TVSum and SumMe) using F1 score and BLEU metrics, the proposed framework demonstrates significant performance improvements of about 3% over baseline methods and prior approaches. The experimental evaluations exhibit substantial advancements in transfer learning scenarios, showcasing its robust generalization capabilities and being adapted to a zero-shot learning setting by training without ground-truth supervision.Our repository of codes is available at this link: https://github.com/hkhitesh7/Video-Summarization-using-CAT.

articleTitle: Enhancing Software-Defined Networks (SDN) Environment to Detect DDoS Attack Using KNN Classifier Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: A new paradigm in network management called Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers improved control and operational capabilities over network infrastructures. At the core of an SDN-based network lies the SDN controller, akin to an operating system, tasked with executing diverse network applications and ensuring the smooth operation of network services and functionalities. Because of its design's inherent complexity, SDN presents several security concerns despite its great potential. One prevalent threat is Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, which are particularly impactful due to the centralized nature of SDN, especially at its control layer, causing network-wide disruptions. Machine learning techniques are being used more to spot risks. By utilizing the NSL-KDD dataset and Linear SVM, Quadratic SVM, and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithms, this paper assesses several feature selection techniques for machine learning in DDoS detection. It highlights the crucial role that optimal feature selection plays in improving classification accuracy and SDN controller performance. According to the testing findings, the KNN classifier provides a 98.41% detection rate for DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: E2FP-Net: Elevated Fusion Feature Pyramid Network for Alzheimer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD), a neurogenerative disorder which is a progressive disease and it affects the cognitive function of the brain and aids in behavioral changes and loss of memory. AD a challenging and a complicated condition in which enhanced diagnosing method, treating method is investigated by the researchers. Treating the symptoms of AD can improve the quality of life to the individuals. Diagnosing methods of AD may include Neuro imaging, CSF analysis, Cognitive testing, Genetic testing etc.., By integrating the MRI images and genetic images we propose an Elevated feature pyramid network based on Adaptive hypergraph neural network. Furthermore, the GNN involves in the process of feature extraction of MRI images and Genomic data. Our proposed framework has the following process for detecting AD: A) Twin data pre-processing B) E2FP based Feature extraction C) Node mingle fusion. The feature extraction process has 3 subprocess includes a) Region based feature extraction for MRI images using Adaptive HGNN b) Mid-Level Feature Extraction for Genomic data using Adaptive HGNN c) Amalgamation of Global Feature. Our model performs well in terms of accuracy, sensitivity and specificity. This model has the achieved a great interpretability in genomic data and by enhancing the contrast the MRI data shows a best accuracy.

articleTitle: Water Quality Parameters Modeling of Thamirabarani River
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: An extensive water quality analysis of the water quality of the Thamirabarani River located in the Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi districts of Tamil Nadu, India, is conducted. This investigation focuses on 28 exclusive water parameters divided into physical, chemical, and biological parameters, including ammonia, biological oxygen demand, pH, and significant indicators. The dataset utilized for this analysis is sourced from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board. This study employs machine learning algorithms inclusive of prediction and classification algorithms. Multiple-Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, Elastic Net regression, Support Vector Machine, k-Nearest Neighbors and Random Forest are used to classify the 5 Designated Best Use classes. These algorithms iterate through various combinations of considered water parameters until convergence for providing accurate insights into their interrelationships. The random forest produces 77% accuracy which is high compared to other algorithms. The outcomes of this research hold significance for policymakers and environmentalists, offering valuable insights into the water quality of the Thamirabarani River.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator
Author Keywords: Accuracy and Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board

articleTitle: Predicting Solar and Wind Power Production with the Weather Map Data Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Signal Processing, Computation, Electronics, Power and Telecommunication (IConSCEPT)
abstract: Renewable energy technologies, such as solar and wind power, play a pivotal role in addressing the growing energy demands of the modern world while mitigating environmental concerns. However, the intermittent and weather-dependent nature of these energy sources presents a significant challenge in harnessing their full potential. This research aims to enhance the precision of forecasting solar and wind power production, thus addressing the current technology deficit in this area. The aim of this research is to develop advanced predictive models that can accurately forecast solar and wind power production. The problem statement is formulated as follows: “To predict solar and wind power generation with high precision by leveraging meteorological data and advanced data analytics techniques.” This research methodology involves the fusion of historical weather data, machine learning algorithms, and time series analysis, specifically employing the comparative predictions of AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and F- Prophet model. The results highlight the successful development of ARIMA and F-Prophet based predictive models for solar and wind power generation. These models exhibit remarkable accuracy in short-term forecasting, demonstrating their effectiveness in addressing the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources. Key numerical results indicate prediction accuracies exceeding 90% for both solar and wind power.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Fourier Series Applications in Music Theory and Practice

abstract: Scholars have been fascinated by the intersection of math and music for centuries, with evolving into a powerful method that can unravel the complex connection between sound and numbers. This paper looks at the deep relationship between Fourier series and music theory including how mathematical ideas like harmonic analysis and frequency synthesis - drive musical composition, performance, audio synthesis among oth-ers. The objective being to demystify the basic components of music through historical insights, case studies, and mathematical analyses. We also explore its historical background in relation to music theory development starting from ancient Chinese dynasties up to modern day use such as compression algorithms for audio.
